description: NVFP4-CB / FP8-CB codebook container, served by the separately released Gridbook plugin pinned in prismaquant/gridbook_runtime/gridbook_runtime_pin.json. PrismaQuant does not vendor the runtime. Load/generation validation is endpoint-driven and has separate eager and graph receipts because Gridbook is installed in an exact-pinned serving container rather than imported into the build environment.

gates.description: Fresh exact-pinned Gridbook container, TP=1, fp8 KV, speculative decode off, --enforce-eager, then two identical non-empty greedy completions over the OpenAI endpoint. Fills the eager load/generation slot, then reuses that exact live nonce-bound session for the independently recorded numeric ship gate and refuses unless the current ship_gate slot replays. It makes no gold-quality or performance claim.

A second fresh exact-pinned Gridbook container with --enforce-eager absent, followed by the same endpoint proof and a distinct server-side fingerprint. Eager success cannot stand in for CUDA-graph load/capture/generation success.

Unchanged from the native lane: same validator, endpoint, and thresholds. For DSv4, serve_dsv4_cb_validate.sh eager invokes it before tearing down the exact nonce-bound server and explicitly verifies the resulting ship_gate slot.

Served KL-vs-BF16 in the plugin serving env. Its BF16 teacher is produced first by tools/build_streamed_full_kl_teacher.py --wikitext-inputs <gold-inputs.json>. Match extension residency across A/B arms: loading a CUDA extension shifts allocator addresses and moves confident-KL by up to 17%.
Direct WikiText PPL on the served CB artifact using the exact CPU-materialized, value-closed offline token payload.

Blocking paired single-Spark proof over the predeclared prefill, decode, and mixed matrix. The candidate must meet the strict phase-specific speed floor against the exact inventory-bound container this release displaces under the same whole-artifact byte budget and serving stack. The manifest states this release-comparison scope explicitly; it does not claim that the displaced container is globally fastest. A native-only infeasibility certificate remains independent and does not substitute for served parity.

kl_evaluator.note: Reachable on this lane since CB Milestone C (R3): the production cache renders CB rungs imatrix-weighted via --col-weights, so a frontier KL measures the bytes the exporter ships. Selection on this lane is still SURROGATE by default — validated-frontier CB selection is enabled, not promoted.

served_activation_quantization.rationale: Gridbook's CB runtime takes the exact native BF16 bridge unless a fused activation mode is selected by a PROCESS-GLOBAL env selector (gridbook/moe.py `_requested_fused_fp4_moe_mode`, gridbook/linear.py PRISMAQUANT_CB_FUSED_FP4). Every gate and gold serve on this lane leaves both unset -- serve_dsv4_cb_validate.sh asserts 'PRISMAQUANT_CB_FUSED_FP4: expected <unset>' -- so no format's activation grid is executed here and every A-side price is exactly zero. The artifact's per-scheme `activation_contract` is PERMISSION for a fused mode, not selection of one; there is no per-unit A4/A16 choice on this lane because the selector is not per-unit.
served_activation_quantization.if_this_changes: Selecting a fused mode makes the A-side REAL and AQUA applicable: list the formats whose activation grid the selected mode executes, and re-price. Do not edit this to silence a refusal.

notes: Required CI compares the producer profiles declared CB-eligible with the pinned Gridbook consumer contract; the preflight refuses any mismatch (R6).
Single-GPU only: the pinned Gridbook contract has no qualified TP path.

The DSv4 driver pins the Spark image by digest and vLLM commit, installs the tracked released Gridbook commit independently in each arm, refuses speculative decode, enforces a post-load memory floor plus watchdog, and records the server-side serve fingerprint.
